title: FSD S5 reads the ACE asset, collateral and score views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05
section: A1.1 constraints, A2.1 to A2.25 integration points and the A2.6, A2.7, A2.8, A2.11, A2.15, A2.16, A2.20, A2.22, A2.23, A2.24, A2.25 field catalog
description: The whole of the asset field catalog names the fields as v_ace_npa_asset.asset_key, asset_ref, asset_code, transfer_in_type, from_segment, transfer_in_date, v_ace_collateral.asset_key and v_ace_asset.asset_type, and the integration points of A2.1, A2.2, A2.3, A2.6, A2.10 and A2.11 name 'ACE (v_ace_npa_asset; RPS, AMIS and CCMS ingested by ACE)' and 'v_ace_score' as a direct read. Arch v5 slide 37 turns '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' into 'views read only by rwb-source-data', slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone, and slide 12 says every service that needs ACE data asks rwb-source-data by REST or by a Temporal activity. Slide 13 gives the S5 row no cell to P1 at all, so the FSD's read path is disallowed and no replacement path is drawn.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.6.3.2, A2.7.3.2, A2.8.3.2, A2.11.3.2, A2.15.3.2, A2.16.3.2, A2.20.3.2, A2.22.3.2, A2.23.3.2, A2.24.3.2 and A2.25.3.2 field catalog rows prefixed v_ace_npa_asset, v_ace_collateral and v_ace_asset; A2.1.2, A2.2.2, A2.3.2, A2.6.2, A2.10.2 and A2.11.2 integration points. Arch v5 slide 12 (need ACE data, ask rwb-source-data), slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views), slide 13 (S5 row: T to P7, E from S4, T E to P8 and S9; no P1 cell). Rules DP-05 and DP-13.
proposed: Carry the FSD field names as the source field names the rwb-source-data contract returns, build every asset, collateral and score read on that contract, and add the missing S5 to P1 cell to the connection matrix. Confirm the contract fields, the business key and the freshness response with P1 before wave 2 system test.

title: The asset record is modelled as an extension of the ACE asset, while Architecture v5 gives rwb-asset the assets taken on
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables and rulings
section: T3.1 object and field definitions; service contract rwb-asset
description: TSD S5 defines the object 'asset (EXTEND ACE Asset)' with id, case_id, collateral_id, asset_ref from AMIS, asset_code, asset_type, transfer_in_type, from_segment, transfer_in_date, book_value, auction_purchase_price, repossessed_date, stock_date, holding_status and holding_cost_to_date, which reads as an extension of an ACE-owned object. Arch v5 slide 18 states that rwb-asset 'writes schema rwb_asset: assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds' and slide 41 states that it owns 'assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds'. The Ownership Map holds no row for an asset table at all, so the service that the architecture gives the take-on record has no table and no stated owner for it.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 asset (EXTEND ACE Asset) and its DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 rows. Arch v5 slide 18 (DB writes schema rwb_asset) and slide 41 (S5 owns assets taken on). Ownership Map Tables: rows for asset_sale and listing owned by S5, no asset row. Arch v5 slide 30 (19 recovery schemas, rwb_asset listed).
proposed: State the holding record as this service's own record in schema rwb_asset, keyed by the ACE asset key with no foreign key and no copied ACE column, and add the asset table row to the Ownership Map in the same change; the ACE asset itself stays read-only through the source-data contract.

title: The Ownership Map lists no table for auction rounds, bids or holding costs, although Architecture v5 and the rules need them
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.5, A2.7, A2.13, A2.15, A2.16, A2.21
section: Service contract, rwb-asset; A2.5.3.1, A2.7.3.1, A2.13.3.1, A2.15.3.1, A2.16.3.1 rules
description: Arch v5 slides 18 and 41 give rwb_asset the auction rounds, and the FSD rules use bid_amount, price_at_round, relist_count, round and holding_cost_to_date, while the TSD records a round only as listing.round_no. The Ownership Map names two S5 tables, asset_sale and listing, and no row for a round, a bid, an award, a holding cost or a work order. Every story's section 12.7 and the DB story are written from that register, so three of the things this product holds have no table to be written into.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 and 41 (rwb_asset: assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds). FSD S5 A2.5.3.1 (holding_cost_to_date), A2.7.3.1 (work order), A2.13/17 (relists), A2.15.3.1 and A2.16.3.1 (bid, round, floor). TSD S5 T3.1 listing DF-SAL-006 round_no. Ownership Map Tables: owner S5 rows asset_sale and listing only.
proposed: Name the round, the bid and the holding-cost movement as entity groups of this service and leave the physical names to the DB story; add the missing rows to the Ownership Map before the S5 DB story starts.

title: AssetSold has no event number and no row in the Ownership Map event sheet
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events
section: Service contract rwb-asset OUT; A3 event catalogue 2/2
description: Arch v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 with AssetTakenOn and AssetSold, and slide 43 carries AssetTakenOn as row 22 with the producer rwb-asset and the consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment. AssetSold appears only in the '+' rows of slide 43 with no EV number. The Ownership Map events sheet holds EV-22 for AssetTakenOn and nothing for AssetSold, so the event the proceeds and the case both depend on has no catalogue identity.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 19 (rwb.asset.events.v1: AssetTakenOn, AssetSold), slide 43 row 22 (EV-22 AssetTakenOn, producer rwb-asset, consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment) and the '+' row (AssetSold, rwb-asset, rwb.asset.events.v1, rwb-payment and rwb-case). Ownership Map Events: EV-22 only for S5.
proposed: Publish AssetSold on rwb.asset.events.v1 as a CloudEvent keyed by asset and case and allocate its EV number and catalogue row in the event catalogue next version; the product requirement does not wait for the number.

title: The round operation and the REST base are named differently on the architecture slide, in the TSD and in the Ownership Map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 appendix T-A; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints and rulings; Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-13
section: Service contract rwb-asset IN; T-A.1 endpoint inventory
description: Arch v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset 'GET/POST /assets, /listings; POST /auction-rounds'. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists API-S5-005 POST /api/recovery/v1/listings/{listingId}/rounds and keeps the monolith base /api/recovery/v1 for all five operations. The Ownership Map rules the business-key paths GET /assets/{assetKey} and POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings as the current ones and records GET /assets/{assetId} and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings as superseded, while it keeps POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds. DP-13 replaces /api/recovery/v1 with /api/recovery/<short>/v1, so three of the four readings of one path set disagree.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 19 (POST /auction-rounds). TSD S5 T-A.1 API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 (all /api/recovery/v1). Ownership Map Endpoints: GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetKey}, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings, POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds current; the two assetId paths superseded under D-RCV-35. Rules DP-13.
proposed: Publish the four current operations under /api/recovery/asset/v1 with the ACE business key, and write the round as a sub-resource of the listing in the contract story; the architecture slide's /auction-rounds is read as the same resource named loosely.

title: The vendor allocation rule is written by distance in the FSD and by scorecard in the FSD's own rule row
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A1.2 FEAT-AST-14 and A2.14.3.1; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-027; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 21
section: A1.2 feature overview; A2.14 Allocate the asset to an auction vendor by distance
description: FEAT-AST-14 reads 'Picks one of the four vendors by distance and capacity, as the current rule does', and BR-027 reads 'the asset is allocated to a vendor by distance and capacity'. Rule R-DIS-30 in the same FSD section reads 'Allocate the asset to the vendor with the highest predicted price on the scorecard, not by distance'. The two statements cannot both be the requirement, and the Temporal design gives the disposal route set 72 rules with the Drools decision unnamed, so the source of truth for the allocation test is not settled.
evidence: FSD S5 A1.2 FEAT-AST-14; A2.14.3.1 R-DIS-30 and R-DIS-31. BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-027 (by distance and capacity). Temporal and Drools Design slide 21 (disposal route set, 72 rules, package Phase 2).
proposed: Keep BR-027's wording as the requirement, state that the allocation rule in force decides between distance and capacity and the scorecard, and record the rule version and the reason with every allocation so either answer is defensible; the rule row is settled with the rule package.

title: The listing must publish to the bank channel and the auction portal, and the bank channel interface does not exist
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 REQ-S5-005; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-014; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.12; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T5.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 45
section: A2.12 Publish the listing; T5.1 external interfaces INT-27
description: REQ-S5-005 and BR-014 require the listing to be published to the bank's channel and the auction portal from one action, and FSD A2.12 says it publishes to HOME.SCB, the EASY app and the auction portal. TSD S5 T5.1 records INT-27 HOME.SCB as 'Not available today; published by the sale officer', and the BRD row for INT-27 repeats it. Arch v5 gives rwb-asset the partner gateway and rwb-partner for vendor instructions and no auction-portal or HOME.SCB interface, so the one action the requirement names cannot reach the bank channel today.
evidence: Program v5 REQ-S5-005; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-014 and the INT-27 row; FSD S5 A2.12.2 integration points (HOME.SCB, auction portals) and A2.12.3.1 R-DIS-33; TSD S5 T5.1 INT-27 (not available today; published by the sale officer); Arch v5 slide 19 (S5 OUT: partner issueInstruction) and slide 45.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Make the one action record the listing, its prices and its schedule and issue the publication to the auction channel through rwb-partner, and record the HOME.SCB publication as an officer step with its date and reference until INT-27 exists; the requirement keeps REQ-S5-005's wording.

title: The E4 vendor allocation depends on a partner capability delivered one wave later
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.14 prerequisites and A1.1 dependencies; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-019 and section 8.6; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json slices RWB-S5-E4023 and RWB-S9-E6029; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38
section: A1.1 dependencies, A2.14 prerequisites
description: FEAT-AST-14 carries the prerequisite FEAT-PRM-03 and the dependency list of A1.1 names it. FEAT-PRM-03 is S9's 'Allocate work by measured return', first in E6, and the slice plan places its delivery in RWB-S9-E6029 at wave 4 with the release 30 April 2027, while the story that needs it, RWB-S5-E4023, sits in wave 3 with the release 28 February 2027. BRD Q-019 asks whether the partner instruction capability belongs to E4 or to E6 and is still open, so the vendor allocation of this service has no delivered dependency at its release.
evidence: FSD S5 A1.1 dependencies (FEAT-PRM-03) and A2.14.2 prerequisites (FEAT-PRM-03). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-019, section 8.6 FEAT-PRM-03 rows. split_plan.json: RWB-S5-E4023-CON and -APP wave 3, release 28 February 2027; RWB-S9-E6029-CON and -APP wave 4, release 30 April 2027. Arch v5 slide 38 (wave 4 adds S9).
proposed: Build the allocation and the instruction against the published rwb-partner contract and its fake, as contract-first delivery requires, so wave 4 does not block wave 3, and answer Q-019 in the same change; until then the allocation is recorded and the instruction is held.

title: The re-appraisal order leaves for SVAF, which Architecture v5 does not connect to this service and gives to rwb-valuation
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.9 and A1.2 FEAT-AST-09; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T5.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 21
section: A2.9 Re-appraise a held asset on cycle; T5.1 INT-11
description: A2.9 orders the re-appraisal 'through SVAF' with INT-11 SVAF as a weekly inbound file load, and the Temporal design makes the re-appraisal step two of the disposal flow with R-DIS-15 and JOB-19. Arch v5 has no SVAF interface and gives the valuations and the valuation order to rwb-valuation (slide 41), the Ownership Map rules both asset valuation operations to S1, and slide 13 gives the S5 row no cell to S1, so the service that must order a re-appraisal has neither an appraiser path nor a valuation owner to call.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.9.2 integration points (SVAF), A1.2 FEAT-AST-09 (raises the re-appraisal order) and A2.9.3.1 R-DIS-15. TSD S5 T5.1 INT-11 SVAF (in, file load, weekly). Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 owns valuations) and slide 13 (S5 row without an S1 cell). Ownership Map Rulings ASM-A6-api-6 (the two asset valuation paths belong to S1). Temporal and Drools slide 21 (re-appraise at 12 months, R-DIS-15, JOB-19).
proposed: Order the re-appraisal through the valuation owner's contract and read the accepted value and its date back through rwb-source-data, add the S5 to S1 cell to the connection matrix, and keep the 12-month interval and the monthly scan as the product behaviour.

title: Proceeds, cost of carry and fees are posted to ALS and the ledger by this service, while Architecture v5 gives posting to rwb-payment
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.5, A2.18, A2.21 and A2.23 integration points; Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T5; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 43 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.5, A2.18, A2.21, A2.23 integration points; service contract rwb-asset TMP line
description: FSD A2.5 names AMIS, ALS and GL, A2.18 names the auction portals, ALS and GL, A2.21 names ALS and GL, and A2.23 names AMIS, ALS and GL as the integration points of this module. Arch v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset the Temporal call 'Payment: postProceeds' and slide 43 gives rwb-payment the producer role for ProceedsMatched, with rwb-asset among its consumers; slide 41 gives rwb-payment the payment and proceeds matching, the fees and the postings. Two owners therefore appear to post the same money.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.5.2, A2.18.2, A2.21.2 and A2.23.2 integration points. Arch v5 slide 19 (S5 OUT TMP: Payment postProceeds), slide 43 row 25 (ProceedsMatched, producer rwb-payment, consumers rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff, rwb-guarantee) and slide 41 (P8 owns payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files).
proposed: Hand every posting to rwb-payment through postProceeds and record the result from ProceedsMatched, so this service holds no ALS interface and no general-ledger interface; the cost of carry is passed to the same call with its period.

title: The pricing agent proposes the route and the price, and Architecture v5 connects this service to no agent
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.10.3.1 R-DIS-19 and A2.11.3.1 R-DIS-28; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events and rulings; Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-20
section: A2.10 Recommend the disposal route; A2.11 Set the start and floor price
description: R-DIS-19 reads 'Pricing agent recommends the disposal route with reasons and the COLLINS economics' and R-DIS-28 reads 'Pricing agent proposes the opening price and the floor price as the reserve'. The slide 13 matrix gives the S5 row no cell to P10, the Ownership Map lists no agent, prompt or run for S5, and DP-20 makes the agent reachable only through the rwb-agent contract, so the two rules that name an agent have no path and no recorded run.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.10.3.1 R-DIS-19 and A2.11.3.1 R-DIS-28. Arch v5 slide 13 (S5 row: T to P7, E from S4, T E to P8 and S9; no P10 cell). Ownership Map Events (no S5 agent event) and Rulings. Rules DP-20.
owner_role: Solution architect with the model risk officer
proposed: Carry the recommendation and the price proposal as decisions of the disposal rule set, and treat the agent as an optional proposer used only through the rwb-agent contract with its 60 s limit, its fallback to the rule result and its run record; record the missing cell.

title: The disposal rule set has 72 rules over 40 states, the FSD names about 40 of them, and the package is Phase 2 with no code
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T4; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.1 to A2.25 rule tables; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 21 and slide 33 notes
section: T4 state machines and workflow; A2 rule tables
description: TSD S5 T4 states 'DISPOSAL. 72 rules over 40 states. The full table is in the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook' and prints 26 of them with 'and 47 more'. The FSD prints about 40 R-DIS rows across the 25 features. The Temporal design names the 'Disposal route set, 72 rules (package Phase 2)' and its third note says the Drools packages for S1 and S3 to S9 exist but the package codes are Phase 2 and each needs an owning service. No source read gives the package code, the remaining rule texts or the 40-state list, so the requirement cannot name the rules it will evaluate.
evidence: TSD S5 T4 (72 rules over 40 states, 26 printed, 'and 47 more'). FSD S5 A2.1.3.1 to A2.25.3.1 (R-DIS-01 to R-DIS-71, unevenly distributed). Temporal and Drools slide 21 (Disposal route set, 72 rules, package Phase 2) and the note to slide 33 (packages exist, codes Phase 2).
proposed: Require the rules as versioned data rows with the package version recorded on every decision, carry the rule texts the FSD states as the requirement, and leave the package code, the remaining rules and the state list to the rule package in rwb-decision.

title: The non performing asset stock balance must have one named owner and no source names the role
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 REQ-S5-002; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-012 and Q-009; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.6
section: A2.6 Record and track the asset stock balance; BR-012; Q-009
description: BR-012 requires that the stock balance 'has one named owner and is reported monthly' and REQ-S5-002 repeats it, with the rationale that the balance has no owner today. FSD A2.6 makes the NPA and asset manager the primary role and the Head of NPA the second, but names no owner. Q-009 asks 'Which role owns the non performing asset stock balance?' of the Head of NPA and is open, so the requirement names a control it cannot yet assign.
evidence: Program v5 REQ-S5-002 (owner column: Head of NPA). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-012 and Q-009. FSD S5 A2.6.1 (gives the stock balance an owner and a number on one screen; it has no owner today) and A2.6.3.3 roles.
proposed: Hold the owner as a role in versioned reference data, refuse to publish the monthly balance where no owner role is in force, and leave the answer to Q-009.

title: The floor approval ladder is named in amounts and percentages whose comparison signs cannot be read
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 21; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL18 and section 9; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.11 and A2.16
section: Temporal and Drools slide 21 'Who approves'; A2.11 Set the start and floor price; A2.16 Accept a bid below the floor
description: The Temporal design gives the approval ladder as 'L5, THB 20m at 70% FMV; PARC, 200m at 70%; MC, 500m at 60%', but the comparison signs on both the amount and the percentage are not readable in the text extract. DL18 leaves every approval level and limit to be loaded from the regulation with names and substitutes to follow, and Q-001 asks for the same. The floor approval of A2.11 and the second signature of A2.16 both depend on it, and VR-S5-011-1 to VR-S5-023-1 test a floor against 'the approver's limit'.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 21 (Who approves: L5 20m at 70% FMV, PARC 200m at 70%, MC 500m at 60%; the comparison glyphs are unreadable in the extract). Program v5 DL18 and section 9. BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001 and BR-028. FSD S5 A2.11.3.1 VR-S5-011-1, A2.16.3.1 and MSG-S5-001.
proposed: Read every floor limit from the versioned delegation table of rwb-access at run time, carry the three amounts and the three percentages as stated, and treat the direction of the test as open until DL18 and Q-001 answer.

title: The classification and the retention of the asset, listing and sale records are not set
source: Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-028, NFR-031 and NFR-047; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL26; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 field catalogs
section: Field catalogs A2.6.3.2 to A2.25.3.2; non-functional retention and classification
description: Every S5 field catalog row carries 'Personal data: No' and no classification, and no S5 source states a retention period. NFR-047 requires a classification on every data product and document type, NFR-028 and NFR-031 require retention classes and periods, and DL26 and Q-012 leave both to Compliance. The records include sale prices, gain and loss, bidder identity and partner fees, so the handling rule cannot be inferred.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.6.3.2 to A2.25.3.2 (Personal data column all 'No'). NFR-028 (retention classes, periods not set), NFR-031 (case record retention, not set), NFR-047 (classification scheme to be applied). Program v5 DL26. BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012.
proposed: Carry the classification stated in section 8 of this PRD, hold the periods as open, and record the classification on every record so a retention load can be applied without a rebuild.

title: No approval is recorded for the requirements this PRD states
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R1 U8, R8.1 and R9; the governance section of the BRDs read for this WP
section: Section 13 Approval
description: This document is status Draft, its approval table is empty, and the BRD it is built from carries no Product Owner decision in the form this WP asks for. Under the realignment run there is no human verification stop, so the missing approval is carried as an assumption rather than as an answer, and no approval is invented.
evidence: Rules R1 U8 (no human verification stops in this run) and R9 (missing value becomes a gap row and an assumption row). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 13 (governance and approval) carries roles and no dated decision for this PRD. This PRD section 13.
proposed: Hold the document at Draft, leave the approval table empty, and record the Product Owner and FDA approval as the next step after this run.

title: The history of FSD S5 versions 1 and 2 is not in the sources read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 document control; 03 Requirements and specifications document list
section: Document control and change note
description: FSD S5 v3 carries one change note, for v3, and no record of v1 or v2 beyond the phrase 'Everything else unchanged from v2'. The folder holds the Functional Specifications by Module v4, v5 and v6 archives, and the earlier S5 versions inside them were not opened or converted for this WP, so their dates and changes are not carried.
evidence: FSD S5 v3 document control (Version 3, 15 November 2026, change note for v3 only). 03 Requirements and specifications folder: Functional Specifications by Module v4.zip, v5.zip, v6.zip.
proposed: Carry v3 in full and mark v1 and v2 as not specified in the sources read; open the earlier archives only if an ID continuity question is raised.

title: The statutory notice and the document evidence have no cell in the connection matrix
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.1, A2.4, A2.20; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13, 16, 17 and 37; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.1 photographs and condition; A2.4 statutory notice (WIN); A2.20 Land Office documents
description: A2.4 serves the statutory notice with WIN as its integration point, A2.1 records photographs and condition of a repossessed vehicle, and A2.20 releases the documents from custody and records the Land Office transfer. Architecture v5 gives notices and their proof of delivery to rwb-comms (slide 17) and documents with write-once custody to rwb-document (slide 16), and states that documents go to Blob with WORM through rwb-document only (slide 37). The slide 13 S5 row has no cell to P6 and no cell to P5, so neither the notice request nor the evidence upload has a drawn path.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.4.2 integration points (WIN), A2.1.3.1 R-DIS-01 (condition, photographs, location), A2.20.3.1 R-DIS-52 (release the documents from custody). Arch v5 slide 12 (call-type decision guide), slide 13 (S5 row without P5 or P6 cells), slide 16 (P5 documents and custody), slide 17 (P6 notices and proof of delivery), slide 37 (Blob WORM through rwb-document only).
proposed: Raise the notice through the rwb-comms contract and read its proof of delivery back as an event, and store every photograph, inspection report and transfer document through the rwb-document contract, recording the missing cells for the matrix.

title: Four of the six messages this module shows belong to other services and the two of its own have no approved wording
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.1 to A2.25 rule and exception tables; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL10; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 across A2.1 to A2.25; MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002 in A2.9 and A2.11 to A2.25
description: The S5 screens and refusals show MSG-P1-001 (stale data product), MSG-P4-002 (role without the right), MSG-P7-003 (decision log unavailable) and MSG-GEN-001 (required field empty), which are the catalogues of P1, P4, P7 and the common set. MSG-S5-001 (floor below the approver's limit) and MSG-S5-002 (appraisal older than a year) are this module's own. DL10 leaves the Thai name of every field, label and message to the business lead with Legal and Compliance, so no wording is settled for either group.

title: The asset population, the auction round volume and the holding cost volume are in no source
source: Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-001 to NFR-007; Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A1.3 and A2 metric tables; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.1
section: A1.3 background and the metric table of each feature; non-functional volume requirements
description: The volume requirements state cases (about 23,600 open at go-live and 26,500 at the end of 2027, from 3,110 new accounts a month), staff users (914 named, about 370 online), partner users (about 320, of 4 auction vendors and 35 buyers), documents and the decision log. No source states how many assets are held, how many rounds are run a month, how many holding cost entries are raised or how many assets reach RAMC, a buy-back, a rental or a broker, so the sizes the performance and capacity tests need cannot be read.
evidence: NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, NFR-004 and NFR-007 (cases, users, documents, decision log). FSD S5 A1.3 (the NPA sales cycle is 1,486 days) and the metric table repeated in A2.1 to A2.25 (target 1,095 days, no volume). Program v5 section 6.1.
owner_role: Solution architect with the data product owner
proposed: Size on the case volume and the NPA book stated in NFR-001 until the asset and round volumes are given, and record the volume as an open question that blocks the performance test only.
